subject: Post-demo recap: Lifecraft model fit & safety probe
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@lifecrafthealth.com>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@lifecrafthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: Lifecraft model fit & safety probe

Hi Sam / Emily — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on what we heard: 

1) Primary goal: triage and summarize patient intake notes for clinical ops (abstractive summaries + structured extraction of meds, allergies, next steps). Sensitive domain: PHI present in free text.

2) Risk posture: Lifecraft wants conservative refusals on diagnosis/prognosis requests; high fidelity extraction for meds/allergies; minimal hallucination on patient identifiers.

3) Recommended initial model candidates (based on latency/cost tradeoff for your expected 2k reqs/day):
   - RW-open-7B-q4 (baseline — good throughput, acceptable refusal tuning)
   - RW-refuse-7B-guard (refusal-calibrated variant for sensitive prompts)
   - RW-13B-std (if you need stronger factual grounding for medication normalization)

4) Eval plan we propose:
   - Short benchmark (500 clinical notes) run against the three variants.
   - Prompt set v1 (attached) includes: extraction probes, refusal triggers, adversarial redaction tests.
   - Metrics: extraction F1 (meds/allergies), hallucination rate (hallucinated PHI), refusal precision/recall.

5) Safety probes: we will include scenario templates that attempt to elicit diagnosis/prognosis. We’ll measure refusal behavior and adjust thresholding rules + output filtering.

Next steps I can take this week:
- Upload the prompt set + a quick config for the benchmark to your shared Drive (attached).
- Run the 500-note pilot and share results in ~72 hours.
- If Lifecraft is happy with the refusal profile, propose a canary plan for Dedicated capacity (with enforced KV caching & stricter rollout).

Attachments: lifecraft_requirements.xlsx (data scope), lifecraft_promptset_v1.txt (raw prompts).

Open questions for you:
- Are we allowed to use a de-identified subset of notes for the pilot? (preferred)
- Any corporate constraints on on-prem vs hosted for this pilot?

Thanks — I’ll queue the benchmark as soon as you confirm the de-id approach.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@lifecrafthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@lifecrafthealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Lifecraft model fit & safety probe

Thanks Ben — this looks great. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We can provide a de-identified dump for the 500-note pilot (will remove direct identifiers but keep structure). Good?
- Ideally we’d like the model to red-flag any content that asks for diagnosis or medical advice to be routed to a clinician-specific workflow instead of producing a refusal text that might confuse end users. Can you include routing suggestions?
- Timeline: can you confirm the 72-hour estimate once you start the run? We have an internal review meeting on 6/24.

If you need anything else from our side, Emily and I will coordinate the data export.

Cheers,
Sam
Director of Clinical Ops | Lifecraft Health
sam.tucker@lifecrafthealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: Lifecraft model fit & safety probe

Ben / Aditya — forwarding Lifecraft's confirmations. Notes for qualification + internal ask: 

- Data: they will provide de-IDed notes (good). Confirmed scale: ~2k requests/day after pilot.
- Safety requirement: must surface a “route-to-clinician” signal rather than an open-ended medical refusal; this will affect output format and our downstream routing hook. We should prototype a structured refusal response schema (e.g., {action: ROUTE_CLINICIAN, reason: "diagnosis_request"}).
- Cost constraint: they are price-sensitive; favor the 7B q4 baseline for pilot but include the refuse-tuned 7B. If extraction F1 < 0.85 on meds we recommend moving to 13B.

Action items (internal):
  1) Ben to run 500-note benchmark on RW-open-7B-q4, RW-refuse-7B-guard, RW-13B-std (benchdriver config in Drive).
  2) Aditya to sketch a structured refusal schema and a small routing hook (webhook payload example) for the canary.
  3) I will draft a short commercial note: pilot pricing + Dedicated canary uplift options.

Ben — once you have the pilot results, ping me and I’ll prep the commercial.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@lifecrafthealth.com>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@lifecrafthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Lifecraft model fit & safety probe

Sam / Emily — good to confirm. Quick status update: 

- We’ve received the de-IDed sample (thank you). I’ve kicked off the 500-note benchmark against the three variants — ETA for results: ~72 hours (will aim for EOD 6/25).
- Included in the run: adversarial refusal probes and extraction scoring. We’ll produce a short CSV with per-note flags plus aggregated metrics.
- Marissa and Aditya are prototyping the structured refusal schema and a routing webhook example (we’ll attach both to the benchmark report).

Deliverables we will share:
- Benchmark report (metrics + example outputs)
- Prompt set (v1 attached) and any suggested prompt refinements to tighten refusal behavior
- Routing webhook payload example and recommended canary rollout (traffic split suggestions).

If Lifecraft wants stronger non-hallucinatory behavior out of the gate, we can recommend a quick run on RW-13B-std; budget permitting it reduces hallucination on medication normalization. Otherwise we’ll start with the 7B pair and calibrate.

Next call: would 6/26 10:00 AM PT work for a 30-minute readout of results?

Thanks — attaching the promptset and the requirements workbook again.

Attachments: lifecraft_promptset_v1.txt, lifecraft_requirements.xlsx

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
